verdict.rationale: USCIS offers its own headless, programmatic rail through the Torch developer platform. It documents a Case Status API and a FOIA/PA request-and-status API, with developer accounts, API keys, a sandbox for test data, and production keys after a demo. These could be called from CI or automation. However, the docs state there is no filing API: core actions like filing forms, paying fees and changing addresses are only available through the account-based myUSCIS web UI. The probes also show the public case-status host and llms.txt return 403 to keyless agents, so automation outside the keyed APIs is walled off. Missing for 10: API coverage for filing, payments and account management; CI/headless-specific guidance (tokens, rate limits, non-interactive auth); keyless agent-readable docs; independent hands-on corroboration of the APIs working in automation.
